cell-background: Use case: scientific-educational. Create ORIGINAL Anatomy game artwork. The attached image is the SOLE STYLE REFERENCE: faithfully preserve its informal university lecture-note drawing aesthetic: dark blue handwritten ink, carefully hatched coloured-pencil anatomy, translucent pink yellow cyan and violet highlighter, cream subtly ruled notebook paper with left binder holes. This is NOT polished vector art. Use modern explanatory hierarchy and large clearly located magnifications for grades 9–10. Portrait 1024x1536. Keep all illustrations and lettering within x100–940 and y70–850; reserve the entire lower 40% (y920–1536) as empty softly ruled paper for draggable pieces. No decorative doodles in the work area. Lettering clear and short; no game UI. Main heading 'Inside & outside'. Upper composition: large closed cutaway CELL at left, blue aqueous interior and a pink double outer lipid boundary, EMPTY interior without nucleus. At right a clearly connected enlarged patch of membrane: round heads touch water on both sides, paired tails point inward. Label 'water-facing heads', 'tails inside'. Below the upper cell diagram a small independently located NUCLEUS cross-section: purple double envelope, pores and coiled DNA; label 'DNA stays inside'. Show a blue arrow from pore to a short RNA strand labelled 'a copied instruction'. Keep nucleus and cell diagrams distinct explanatory views.

Lettering clear and short; no game UI. Main heading 'Bones & pulling muscles'. Draw ONE SINGLE arm in side view with shoulder/scapula at x480 y230, elbow at x510 y550, forearm slightly angled leftward reaching wrist x470 y850. One humerus (x500), radius and ulna distinct. Biceps belly RED/PINK at x390 y380, triceps VIOLET at x600 y380, both thick spindle shapes with tapered white fibrous tendons: biceps shoulder-to-radius attachment in front of elbow; triceps shoulder/humerus-to-olecranon on back of ulna. Keep muscle bellies lateral to bones so each muscle can be removed without revealing missing bones. White tendons remain distinct outside coloured bellies. Radius small coloured golden mineral window x455 y690; ulna mineral window x535 y720; bone remains visible around each window. Label 'biceps: bends' left, 'triceps: straightens' right, 'radius' left and 'ulna' right with short leaders. Locate a small bone-matrix inset far left at y650 showing fibres, cells and mineral crystals. Inset right y650 shows cells joining to form long striped muscle fibres. Compose clean, anatomically educational; do not draw a second arm.
